concepts.def: Free national health service launched 5 July 1948
Labour minister who set up the NHS in 1948
1942 plan to fight the 'five giants' including disease
Targeted drugs — Salvarsan 606 in 1909 against syphilis

walkthroughs.body_html:
In 1928 Alexander Fleming noticed Penicillium mould killing bacteria on a Petri dish.

He couldn't make enough to test on humans. In 1941 Florey and Chain mass-produced it. US factories made tonnes by D-Day in 1944, saving thousands of Allied soldiers.

The 1942 Beveridge Report attacked five giants: want, disease, ignorance, squalor and idleness.

After Labour's 1945 win, Aneurin Bevan launched the NHS on 5 July 1948 — free at the point of use, paid for by taxes. It was the world's first fully nationalised health service.

In 1909 Ehrlich's Salvarsan 606 was the first 'magic bullet' drug, targeting syphilis.

Later came DNA discovery in 1953, keyhole surgery and the 2003 Human Genome Project. Lifestyle diseases like cancer and heart disease became the new battlefront.
